messages:
sara (support): FYI customer reported retries from our TS SDK causing duplicate charges when requests time out then succeed on retry. They said Node 18, undici 5.x, sdk-js 0.9. Can we triage?
ian (backend): Thanks — do we know whether the retry happened client-side (SDK) or server-side? Need request IDs and any error logs.
matt (sdk-pm): Our SDK v0.9 had an opt-in retry on network errors and used AbortController to cancel fetch. There was an undici change ~5.7 about how aborted requests surface. If their AbortController rejects after successful response commit it could be messy.
sara (support): Customer paste (redacted):
```
RequestId: req_01G...\nstatus: 502 then 200
client: SDK-js@0.9.3
node: v18.12.1
undici: 5.6.2
```
ian (backend): 502 then 200 suggests gateway returned error then succeeded. If SDK immediately retried and original actually processed, they could have two side-effecting calls. Does our API use idempotency-key for that endpoint?
matt (sdk-pm): Not by default for text generation. We expect callers to provide idempotency-key for chargeable endpoints. That said, SDK retry policy should avoid retries if response body came back but the client lost connection. undici behavior: aborting during body stream can still mean server accepted. Older undici versions sometimes surface an aborted socket as fetch error even after 200.
ryan (eng-oncall): Repro plan: replicate node/undici combo and force a race where server returns 200 but connection reset before client reads final chunk. SDK should treat that as success if headers+status arrived, or conservative no-retry? Which behavior do we want?
matt (sdk-pm): We intentionally made retries for 'network' errors only, not on application-level 5xx. But the bug is misclassifying an aborted stream as network error. We'll need to update classification logic: if status code present -> do not retry.
sara (support): Customer wants refund; billing-bot, any way to locate duplicate charges? billing-bot: Found two charges linked to req_01G... and duplicate metadata on both. We've issued refund for the later one and flagged account.
sara (support): Back to engineering: customer attached a short repro using undici fetch and manual AbortController. They simulated by closing socket after headers. Code snippet they used: 
```
const controller = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal });
// simulate socket drop
controller.abort();
```
ian (backend): That sequence is unrealistic because abort() cancels before read. But if network drops after headers but before body, fetch may still resolve headers in some implementations. Need to reproduce with server that delays body.
matt (sdk-pm): Action items for SDK: (1) patch retry classifier to require absence of response status to trigger retry, (2) add advisory in changelog about undici versions <5.8, (3) add opt-in idempotency helper for generation endpoints.
ryan (eng-oncall): I'll try local repro matrix: Node 16/18/20 x undici 4.x/5.6/5.8 x sdk 0.9/1.0. Will post minimal repro thread.
sara (support): Can we send customer a safe workaround? Temporary fix: pin undici >=5.8 or downgrade SDK to 1.x beta?
matt (sdk-pm): SDK 1.x already switched to a fetch wrapper that avoids treating aborted body reads as network error. For 0.9 users: suggest upgrading SDK or set a request-level idempotency-key. Also avoid automatic retries for chargeable endpoints for now.
sara (support): I'll share upgrade + idempotency recommendation and note refund done.
ian (backend): For server-side mitigations we can accept duplicate calls gracefully: dedupe by client-provided idempotency or server-side best-effort check for close timestamps + payload hash. I'll open a small infra task.
ryan (eng-oncall): Quick note — undici 5.7 changed 'body' streaming errors. I'll attach links after I run tests.
matt (sdk-pm): Created GH issue sdk-js#482 describing classifier change and a tests PR.
sara (support): Thanks team. Customer is OK with upgrade plan; keeping thread open until SDK patch released. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC (sdk-js classifier hotfix).
